result.question:
Conduct an exhaustive A-to-Z analysis of the review-automation / online-reputation-management software niche, focused on HOME-SERVICES businesses (HVAC, roofing, plumbing, electrical). This is competitive + market research for TableTurnerr, a new review-automation product for home-services pros (multi-platform review requests via SMS/email triggered by completed jobs, CRM integrations with Jobber/Housecall Pro/ServiceTitan/Workiz/QuickBooks, technician leaderboards, map-pack rank tracking, AI review replies, widgets, auto social posting).

Cover in detail and don't miss anything:
1) FULL competitive landscape — every notable player: Birdeye, Podium, NiceJob, GatherUp, Grade.us, Reviews.io, Signpost, Broadly, Swell, Reputation.com, PulseM, Reviewability, ReviewHarvest, Housecall Pro/Jobber/ServiceTitan/Workiz built-in review tools, Thryv, Weave, plus any others. For each: positioning, target customer, key features, pricing (with numbers if findable), strengths, weaknesses/gaps, and whether they target home services specifically.
2) Table-stakes features vs real differentiators (multi-platform requests, SMS/email, CRM/field-service integrations, review monitoring & alerts, AI-generated replies, technician/employee leaderboards, review gating vs compliance, website widgets, social auto-posting, local rank/map-pack tracking, missed-call text-back, payments/messaging bundling).
3) Pricing models and typical price points across the niche (and where the value/price sweet spot is for small home-services shops).
4) The field-service CRMs (Jobber/Housecall Pro/ServiceTitan) — are their built-in review features competitors or integration partners? How good are they?
5) Compliance & risk: Google's review-gating policy, FTC rules on reviews, TCPA/A2P 10DLC for SMS — what's allowed and what gets accounts/listings penalized.
6) Competitor GTM + SEO playbooks: lead magnets (free review-score/grader tools), content/blog, comparison/"alternative" pages, partnerships, pricing transparency.
7) Underserved gaps and concrete opportunities where a focused, affordable, home-services-only review-automation product can beat the generalists and the CRM built-ins.

Deliver a detailed, cited report with: a competitor comparison matrix, a feature table-stakes vs differentiators breakdown, pricing table, the compliance do's/don'ts, and a prioritized list of what TableTurnerr should do (product + GTM) to win this niche.
result.summary: The home-services review-automation niche is dominated by horizontal generalists (Birdeye, Podium, Broadly) priced for multi-location enterprises, a few transparent home-services-leaning specialists (NiceJob, GatherUp), and the field-service CRMs themselves (Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan via Birdeye), whose built-in review tools are direct but narrow competitors. The product is largely commoditized at the feature level: job-completion-triggered SMS+email review requests, CRM integrations, multi-platform monitoring, AI replies, widgets, and social auto-posting are now table stakes (GatherUp ships all of them from $99/mo; Birdeye/Housecall Pro auto-trigger requests on job completion). The clearest pricing wedge is the affordable, transparent, month-to-month tier ($75-$125/mo, no contract) that NiceJob occupies, versus Birdeye's $299-$449/mo per-location, 12-month auto-renewal contracts plus $5K-$15K implementations. The largest strategic and legal constraint is compliance: review gating is explicitly banned by both Google and the FTC, and SMS requests fall under TCPA/2025 opt-out rules requiring revocation honored within 10 business days. The opportunity for TableTurnerr is a home-services-only, affordable, contract-free, compliance-clean product that beats the CRM built-ins on platform breadth and the generalists on price, transparency, and vertical focus (technician leaderboards, map-pack tracking).

findings.claim: Job-completion-triggered review requests via SMS and email through CRM integration are an established, table-stakes pattern in this niche, offered by both standalone platforms (Birdeye) and the field-service CRMs themselves (Housecall Pro).
findings.evidence: Birdeye's ServiceTitan integration 'Send[s] review requests to your customers automatically after a service order has been completed' and survey requests 'via email and SMS automatically,' built on a documented 'Job Completed' trigger. Housecall Pro's native Reviews feature is 'automatically configured by default to send Review Requests when you click or tap Finish within a Job,' sending both email and text. This confirms the core TableTurnerr feature (job-triggered multi-channel requests) is already standard.

findings.claim: The field-service CRMs are direct competitors, not just integration partners, but their built-in review tools have a narrower multi-platform footprint than full-featured review platforms.
findings.evidence: Housecall Pro's built-in review automation supports only three destinations: Google, Facebook, and the HCP Website (for Website Pros only) - no Yelp, BBB, or Angi. Owners can split request percentages across only those three. Birdeye, by contrast, supports many more destinations and is listed in the ServiceTitan Marketplace as 'the leading AI-powered reputation management platform for home services.' The CRMs compete on convenience/bundling but lose on platform breadth, which is an exploitable gap.

findings.claim: Birdeye is an enterprise/multi-location-targeted AI reputation and social platform (150,000+ businesses) with high pricing, annual auto-renewal contracts, and significant implementation costs.
findings.evidence: Positioned as 'the leading AI-powered reputation and social media management platform for local brands,' used by 150,000+ businesses. Pricing: Starter $299/mo (single location), Growth $349/mo and Dominate $449/mo per location, billed annually with 12-month auto-renewal, plus reported $5,000-$15,000 implementation costs for multi-location rollouts (single-location onboarding $500-$1,500). Targets 10+ location enterprises ('whether you have 10 or 10,000 locations'). The price/contract structure is a clear vulnerability for small home-services shops.
findings.vote: high (claim 8 was 2-1; claim 18 was 2-1; pricing corroborated by multiple aggregators)

findings.claim: NiceJob is the closest affordable, transparent, home-services-leaning specialist competitor: $75/mo and $125/mo, month-to-month with no contract and a 14-day free trial, with native CRM integrations.
findings.evidence: NiceJob's pricing page lists Reviews/Grow at $75/mo and Pro at $125/mo, 'no contracts, no credit card up front,' 14-day free trial. Native integrations with Jobber, Housecall Pro, FieldPulse, and QuickBooks (closing a job auto-triggers a review request). It runs a dedicated home-services landing page ('Perfect for HVAC, plumbing, window cleaning, landscaping'). Caveat: it is horizontal, not exclusively home services, and uses a review funnel that filters negative feedback before public submission - a gating-style mechanism that carries compliance risk.

findings.claim: GatherUp is a transparently-priced full-featured competitor whose all-plan feature set defines the current table-stakes baseline.
findings.evidence: Small Business plan $99/mo (1 location, 14-day free trial); Multi-Location $60/mo per location for 2-10 locations, scaling through tiers up to 101+ locations (no contracts/termination fees). All plans bundle up to 300 SMS + 3,000 email credits per location/month, review monitoring across 100+ sites, NPS surveys, QR codes, API/Zapier, custom AI-generated responses (SmartReply/AutoReply), review widgets/badges, and automated social sharing. This is the feature bar any new entrant must clear.

findings.claim: Broadly targets small service-providing businesses (including home services) as an AI review/reputation tool, now expanded into an all-in-one platform.
findings.evidence: Broadly is 'an online review & reputation management tool that helps small service-providing businesses improve their online reputation,' marketed as 'the all-in-one AI platform that helps local service businesses stand out on Google, earn 5-star reviews' with an 'AI Reputation Specialist' for review responses/requests, explicitly targeting home services, pet, automotive, law, and dental. Note: a specific Broadly home-services-primary positioning at $199-$349/mo was REFUTED, so exact pricing/primary-vertical claims are uncertain.

findings.claim: Swell is a healthcare/patient-experience platform, not a home-services competitor - useful for scoping who is NOT in this niche.
findings.evidence: Swell brands itself the '#1 Patient experience platform for Healthcare,' purpose-built for DSOs, MSOs, and PE-backed specialty groups, integrating with EHR/PMS systems (Dentrix, Open Dental, AthenaHealth). Its user base is overwhelmingly medical and it explicitly does not serve HVAC/plumbing/roofing. It should be excluded from the home-services competitive set.

findings.claim: Review gating is explicitly prohibited by both Google and the FTC - a hard compliance constraint that several competitors' 'review funnel' designs flirt with.
findings.evidence: Google's Maps UGC policy prohibits 'discourag[ing] or prohibit[ing] negative reviews, or selectively solicit[ing] positive reviews,' and bans paying/incentivizing reviews via discounts or free goods; Google removed 292M+ policy-violating reviews in 2025 and may take down even genuine reviews when authenticity is uncertain. The FTC's January 2022 marketer guidance states companies 'should not only ask for reviews from people they think will leave positive ones,' later hardened into the binding FTC Final Rule on Consumer Reviews (effective Oct 2024). NiceJob-style funnels that route negatives privately are a documented gray-area risk.

findings.claim: SMS review requests are governed by TCPA opt-out rules effective April 11, 2025: revocation can be made 'in any reasonable manner' (including STOP/QUIT/END/REVOKE/OPT-OUT/CANCEL/UNSUBSCRIBE), must be honored within 10 business days, and applies to both calls and texts regardless of medium.
findings.evidence: FCC Order 24-24 (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10)): consumers may revoke prior express consent in any reasonable manner; the seven listed keywords are a 'per se reasonable means'; businesses must process opt-outs within a reasonable time not to exceed 10 business days; revocation 'extends to both robocalls and robotexts regardless of the medium.' The broader cross-program 'revoke-all' provision was delayed (to Jan 31, 2027) but the 10-day and keyword rules are in effect. TableTurnerr's SMS engine must implement automatic STOP-handling and 10-business-day suppression, plus A2P 10DLC registration.

result.caveats: Pricing figures are time-sensitive (2025-2026) and partly self-reported vendor marketing; verify on live pricing pages before publishing. Birdeye's $5,000-$15,000 implementation figure applies to multi-location rollouts (single-location is ~$500-$1,500) and rests on secondary/blog sources rather than primary docs (claim was 2-1). Podium pricing/BBB-rating claims were REFUTED and are NOT included here - treat Podium specifics as unverified. Broadly's exact pricing ($199-$349) and 'primary home-services' positioning were also refuted; only its general small-service-business review focus is confirmed. Several non-trivial named competitors in the original brief were NOT verified in any surviving claim: Reputation.com, PulseM, Reviewability, ReviewHarvest, Signpost, Thryv, Weave, Grade.us, Reviews.io, Reviewability, Workiz/Jobber built-in review tools - their positioning, features, and pricing remain open. The 'multi-platform footprint' gap for Housecall Pro is well-sourced; equivalent depth on ServiceTitan/Jobber native review tools is thinner. GTM/SEO playbook details (lead magnets, comparison pages, free grader tools) and the specific differentiators of technician leaderboards / map-pack rank tracking were not independently verified in the surviving claims.
openQuestions: What are the verified current pricing, contract terms, and home-services positioning of the unverified players (Podium, Thryv, Weave, Signpost, Reputation.com, PulseM, Reviewability, ReviewHarvest, GatherUp competitors)? Several were named in the brief but none survived verification.

How good are the NATIVE review tools inside Jobber, ServiceTitan, and Workiz specifically (vs Housecall Pro, which is well-documented)? Are they integration partners or direct competitors, and what platforms do they support?

Do any competitors implement compliant alternatives to review gating, and how does NiceJob's negative-feedback-filtering funnel hold up against Google's and the FTC's bans in practice (enforcement examples)?

What concrete GTM/SEO tactics (free review-grader lead magnets, 'X alternative' comparison pages, CRM-marketplace partnerships, pricing transparency) are competitors actually winning with, and which differentiators (technician leaderboards, map-pack rank tracking, missed-call text-back) are genuinely rare vs commoditized?

refuted.claim: GatherUp does not target home services or any specific industry vertical in its pricing/positioning, serving small businesses, multi-location companies, and agencies generally.
Housecall Pro and Jobber both include built-in review automation (automated review requests and customer follow-ups) as a standard feature of their field-service CRM platforms.
Broadly is positioned as an all-in-one webchat/SMS/review platform that primarily targets home services, local agencies, and independent retailers, priced at $199-$349/month depending on industry.

Among the major Podium alternatives Birdeye lists, only Broadly explicitly emphasizes home services in its positioning; the others (Birdeye, ReviewTrackers, BrightLocal, Reputation.com, SOCi, Yext) do not.

Podium is an omnichannel messaging platform priced at $399/mo (Core, single location) and $599/mo per location (Pro), with add-ons including $99/month for AI replies, 12-month auto-renewal contracts, and a D- BBB rating tied to contract cancellation complaints.
